newsitem.title: USA: Nine die on icy roads in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Nine die on icy roads in Texas.

text.p: At least nine people died in car accidents on icy Texas highways after a winter storm swept through the state over the weekend and dumped up to six inches of snow, officials said on Monday.
Texas Department of Public Safety spokeswoman Sheri Deatherage-Green told reporters the nine deaths occurred in seven separate accidents on Sunday in central and west Texas.
"All these were specifically related to slick roads," she said.

Two people died and two others were injured in Callaghan County near Abilene, Texas when a car traveling west on Interstate 20 slid on ice and snow into the opposite lane and hit an oncoming car, Deatherage-Green said.
Another head-on accident killed one person and critically injured six others near Fredericksburg, Texas 70 miles (112 km) west of Austin, she said.

Overnight snows and freezing rain created hazardous road conditions from near Austin north into Oklahoma, police said. In Dallas and the surrounding area, dozens of accidents were reported Monday morning as commuters tried to go to work.

At Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, American Airlines cancelled 70 flights on Sunday and another 70 early on Monday. An airline spokesman said the cancellations affected about 35 percent of its schedule.
Road crews were out in many places spreading sand on ice-covered bridges to improve traction, the Texas Department of Transportation said.
A DPS dispatcher in Waco, Texas warned that "the roads are very hazardous. They are open, but extremely dangerous."
The heaviest snows were reported in the hill country west of Austin where up to six inches of snow blanketed some areas, said U.S. Weather Service technician Eva Mullen in San Angelo, Texas.
"We got us a nice little Canadian blast," she said of the storm.
Mullen said skies were expected to clear across most of the state on Monday, but that snow still covered the ground in many places and that a hard freeze was expected Monday night.
